## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical batch-job composition: init tooling, config-driven scripts, and safe cleanup. 

## Key Concepts
- Kubernetes Job TTL, backoff, and completion semantics
- InitContainers alongside main containers
- ConfigMap and Secret mounts; env from Secret
- Resource requests/limits; idempotence

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: db-migrate
  namespace: migrate
spec:
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 600
  backoffLimit: 3
  completions: 1
  parallelism: 1
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache postgresql-client"]
      containers:
        - name: migrate
          image: postgres:15
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: db-creds
          env:
            - name: PGHOST

          volumeMounts:
            - name: migrate-scripts

        - name: migrate-scripts
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement a practical, namespace-scoped canary upgrade using standard CKAD tools: CronJob scheduling, patching Deployments, ConfigMaps/Secrets for config and credentials, and PVC-based logging. It also exercises InitContainers, probes, and network policy considerations in a real workflow.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scheduling and JobTemplate execution
- Patching Deployment images with kubectl set image or patch
- Reading image tag from ConfigMap and registry authentication via Secret
- Persisting status in a ConfigMap and logging to a PVC
- InitContainer to install tooling (kubectl, jq)
- Readiness/Liveness probes for the Job Pod
- Namespace NetworkPolicy restricting registry egress

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: canary-upgrade
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: canary-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: alpine:3.17
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq; true"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          containers:
          - name: upgrader
            image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
            command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "set -e; CANARY_TAG=$(kubectl get configmap canary-config -o jsonpath='{.data.tag}'); kubectl patch deployment my-app -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"my-app","image":"myrepo/my-app:${CANARY_TAG}"}]}}}}' --record; echo done; sleep 1"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          imagePullSecrets:
          - name: registry-credentials
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to implement idempotent patches and roll back on failure?
- How to measure canary success (latency, error rate) before full rollout?
- How would this scale across many namespaces or deployments?

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests hands-on CKAD skills: in-cluster configuration, API access, and multi-resource coordination. It evaluates how the candidate wires ConfigMaps, Secrets, and PVCs into a Deployment, and how they enforce traffic restrictions with a NetworkPolicy.

## Key Concepts

- Namespace-scoped Deployment and RBAC permissions
- ConfigMap-based thresholds and Secret-based credentials
- API access to Namespace ResourceQuota metrics
- InitContainer usage for tools like curl/jq
- Logs persisted to a PVC mounted at /logs
- Readiness and liveness probes
- Namespace NetworkPolicy to restrict egress to the central endpoint

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: alert-config
data:
  cpu-threshold: "80"
  memory-threshold: "85"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: alert-credentials
data:
  api-key: <base64-encoded-key>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: log-storage
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: resource-watcher
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: resource-watcher
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: resource-watcher
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: busybox
          command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |-
                wget -q https://github.com/stedolan/jq/releases/download/jq-1.6/jq-linux64 -O /usr/local/bin/jq
                chmod +x /usr/local/bin/jq
                apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /usr/local/bin
      containers:
        - name: watcher
          image: your-watcher-image:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
              name: http
          env:
            - name: CENTRAL_ENDPOINT
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: alert-credentials
                  key: api-key
          volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            - name: config
              mountPath: /config
              readOnly: true
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 5
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
          resources:
            requests:
              memory: "64Mi"
              cpu: "50m"
            limits:
              memory: "128Mi"
              cpu: "100m"
      volumes:
        - name: logs
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: log-storage
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: alert-config
        - name: tools
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: egress-restriction
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: resource-watcher
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              name: central-monitoring
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 443
```

## Trade-offs

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design per-namespace automation with auditability and tight network controls. Image provenance is a critical security concern for multi-tenant environments like Discord or Airbnb, where ensuring container images come from trusted registries is essential.

## Key Concepts
- **CKAD Scheduling**: CronJob for recurring audit tasks
- **Image Provenance**: Registry API integration, image digests (SHA256)
- **Secrets & ConfigMaps**: REGISTRY_TOKEN for authentication, audit-status for state tracking
- **PV-backed Storage**: PVC at /audit for persistent digest reports
- **InitContainers**: Installing required tools (curl, jq) for image inspection
- **Readiness Probes**: Ensuring the pod is ready before accepting traffic
- **Namespace NetworkPolicy**: Restricting egress to only trusted registries

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: image-provenance-audit
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  schedule: "*/30 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: audit-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: tools
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: audit-volume
              mountPath: /audit
          containers:
          - name: auditor
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "..."]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: audit-volume
              mountPath: /audit
            - name: registry-token
              mountPath: /secrets
              readOnly: true
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ["sh", "-c", "[ -f /audit/ready ]"]
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
          volumes:
          - name: audit-volume
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: audit-pvc
          - name: registry-token
            secret:
              secretName: REGISTRY_TOKEN
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: audit-status
  namespace: target-namespace
data:
  last_run: ""
  digest_count: "0"
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: registry-egress
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: registry
```

## Trade-offs Discussion
- **CronJob vs Job**: CronJob provides scheduling but has slight timing drift; use precise timing if required.
- **PVC Size**: Allocate sufficient storage based on pod count and audit frequency.
- **InitContainer Overhead**: Adds startup time but ensures tools are available; consider using a custom image with pre-installed tools.
- **NetworkPolicy Scope**: A permissive egress may be necessary if multiple registries are used; balance security with operational flexibility.
